extraction.name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
extraction.description: A comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing. VoiceAssistant-Eval comprises 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories. These tasks include natural sounds, music, and spoken dialogue for listening; multi-turn dialogue, role-play imitation, and various scenarios for speaking; and highly heterogeneous images for viewing.
extraction.creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li (CUHK MMLab, SenseTime Research, CPII under InnoHK)
extraction.citeAs: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li. VoiceAssistant-Eval: Benchmarking AI Assistants Across Listening, Speaking, and Viewing. arXiv:2509.22651v1 [cs.CL] 26 Sep 2025
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data collection involved extracting diverse visual and auditory inputs from 37 datasets, including natural sounds, music, dialogue, and various images. For role-play tasks, texts from RoleBench were used and 100 distinct roles were selected with three representative audio clips per role. Speech instructions were synthesized using three advanced text-to-speech (TTS) models: F5-TTS, ChatTTS, and Dia-1.6B. The synthesized audio was evaluated with UTMOS and regenerated if scores were below 3.8. Audio was transcribed with Whisper-Large-v3 and only recordings with the lowest word error rates were retained.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source data was collected from 47 datasets spanning audio understanding (23 datasets including LibriSpeech, Common Voice, Clotho, AudioCaps, AVQA for speech, sound, and music), text datasets (22 datasets including RoleBench for role-play tasks), and vision datasets (MMMU covering 30 disciplines and 30 image formats). Specific sources include: For Speech: LibriSpeech, CoVoST 2, Clotho, MELD, SLURP, VoxCeleb1, FoR, Fisher, SpokenWOZ, IEMOCAP. For Sound: AudioGrounding, VocalSound, CochlScene, TUT2017, AVQA, Clotho-AQA. For Music: AudioCaps, MTJ-Jamendo, MUSIC-AVQA, MusicCaps. For General: AudioCaps, AIR-Bench, CommonVoice.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Text instructions were converted into audio using three TTS models. Texts were preprocessed to ensure high synthesis quality: (1) Image references were replaced with descriptive phrases (e.g., '<image1>' became 'as shown in the first image'); (2) Text was rewritten using Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct to ensure challenging content like numbers and mathematical expressions were read accurately (e.g., 'OC=2rsin(π)' became 'O C equals two r times sine of pi'); (3) Multiple-choice options were rephrased for better readability (e.g., '[Man, Woman]' became 'Man or Woman?').
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A multi-stage curation process was conducted: (1) Deduplication: Lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance were used to flag potential duplicates, which were manually reviewed and removed, resulting in 15,359 samples. (2) Validation: Incomplete or unsuitable instances were excluded, including entries with corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, and demonstrably incorrect answers. Approximately 10% of candidates were discarded at this stage. (3) Categorization: Remaining problems were assigned to 13 predefined task categories based on source metadata. (4) Sampling: Data was sampled from categorized problems to balance the ratio of different tasks, resulting in 10,497 high-quality samples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For evaluation, gpt-oss-20b was used to assess response texts with thirteen evaluator prompts. For emotion tasks, emotion2vec was used to get emotion probabilities for angry, disgusted, fearful, happy, neutral, sad, and surprised, keeping all emotions with probabilities larger than 1% in the prompts. The model judger identified essential elements of each task, compared model outputs with reference answers, and delivered a final judgment. For role-play tasks, Wespeaker was used to calculate speaker similarity between model-generated speech and reference role audio.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A lightweight web-based curation tool was built for validation. The tool ingests candidate items consisting of unique ID, metadata, raw prompt, reference answer(s), and associated media (audio waveform(s), image(s), and optional multi-turn transcripts). Curators review each item on a single screen with inline players and viewers, transcripts, and multiple-choice options, then assign a Good or Bad verdict with optional notes.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human evaluation validation was conducted on 10% of Qwen2.5-Omni-7B's responses (1,050 examples) from each of the 13 tasks. Pearson correlation coefficients between gpt-oss-20b scores and human ratings ranged from 0.73 to 1.00 (overall 0.92), with agreement rates uniformly high (often above 90%, overall 96.1%). Stability testing showed evaluation scores were highly consistent across ten repeated runs, with most standard deviations below 3. Statistical significance testing using paired two-sided t-tests with Bonferroni correction confirmed performance differences between models.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: For role-play tasks, three representative audio clips per role were collected. For speech synthesis, multiple TTS models generated audio and only the sample with the lowest word error rate was retained. Human evaluation involved independent review by judges on 10% of samples.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: gpt-oss-20b (for content quality assessment), emotion2vec (for emotion probability extraction), UTMOS (for speech quality measurement), Whisper-Large-v3 (for speech transcription), Wespeaker (for speaker similarity calculation), Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (for text rewriting during preprocessing)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Code and data will be released at the project page. The dataset and code are under an MIT license. A data governance process for auditing and removal is maintained, with the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: For role-play tasks, 100 distinct roles were selected with associated voice profiles. The benchmark includes speaker timbre evaluation and voice personalization tasks. Strict consent, provenance, and anti-impersonation safeguards are emphasized. The paper prohibits training or releasing models intended to reproduce identifiable speakers without documented consent, requires downstream users to implement consent gating and watermarking or traceability of synthetic audio, and provides safety cards describing acceptable use, known risks, and red-team tests for voice cloning abuse.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark addresses critical gaps in evaluating voice assistants for real-world applications including healthcare, education, smart homes, customer service, and automotive industry. It emphasizes hands-free interaction crucial for safety-critical and accessibility-oriented contexts such as driving, operating machinery, or supporting visually impaired users. The evaluation framework aims to guide development of next-generation AI assistants that are trustworthy, reliable, and capable of personalized, multimodal interaction.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is primarily in English, with only five Chinese roles in the role-play task, which may not capture the full variability of real user interactions across diverse linguistic settings. Role-play tasks use a fixed set of 100 roles and associated style prompts which may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas. Questions and contexts are drawn from academic or synthetic sources which might not reflect the full richness or fairness concerns of real deployments.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset size (10.5K curated QA items) may be limited in diversity. All prompts and evaluations except five Chinese roles are in English, limiting generalization to multilingual settings. The benchmark evaluates models in an offline, static manner and does not measure reaction time, ability to handle partial utterances, or barge-in and error recovery. Video-audio integration and continuous audio-visual streaming tasks are beyond the scope. The evaluation relies on automated measures and GPT-based scoring which may introduce noise and bias. Current evaluations do not capture all aspects of human preferences and may favor certain phrasings or overlook nuanced errors.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluating voice assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing capabilities. Use cases include: Testing (comprehensive evaluation of AI assistants on 13 task categories), Validation (assessing model performance on audio understanding, speech generation, and multimodal integration), Fine Tuning (identifying weaknesses to guide model improvement). The benchmark is designed for researchers to better evaluate voice assistants and facilitate future studies. It is not supposed to be used for training models for cheating, though the risk exists. Usage guidelines emphasize strict consent and anti-impersonation safeguards for voice cloning tasks.
